newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador trade deficit falls in Jan-May period.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador trade deficit falls in Jan-May period.

text.p: El Salvador's trade deficit through May was $436.5 million, down from $576.9 million in the first five months of 1996, the Central Reserve Bank said in a report on Thursday.
Exports grew by 40 percent over that time frame to $1.056 billion while imports grew by 12.1 percent to $1.493 billion, the central bank report said.
The manufacturing sector led the way with $403.2 million worth of goods sold abroad through May, up 40.9 percent from the January-to-May period of 1996.
Traditional exports totalled $357.2 million, up from $219.6 million from the first five months of 1996. Coffee represented $304.1 million of the traditional exports from January to May of this year.
Non-traditional exports reached $295.7 million through May, up from $248.5 million in the same period last year.
